notes: No open kb/Work note owns the fix. §1985:VI.6.13.2 prints EVALUATE, one or more selection subjects joined by ALSO (identifier, literal, expression, TRUE, FALSE), one or more groups of WHEN phrases each ending in imperative-statement-1, an optional "[WHEN OTHER imperative-statement-2]" and an optional END-EVALUATE; a selection object is ANY, a condition, TRUE, FALSE, or [NOT] before an identifier, literal or arithmetic expression with an optional THROUGH or THRU second operand, and nothing else. Implemented at 85: evaluateStatement, evaluateWhenClause, evaluateWhenPhrase and evaluateWhenOther hold the shape at every edition (an EVALUATE with only WHEN OTHER, WHEN OTHER twice or not last, a WHEN group with no statement, a missing subject, two objects without ALSO and a doubled THRU are refused; NOT before ANY, TRUE or FALSE is refused by EvaluateBinder.ScreenObjectNegation, COBOL3710), and the later editions' additions that are gated reach 1985: boolean-expression subjects and objects (VisitEvaluateSubject and VisitEvaluateWhenItem, COBOL0900 below 2002) and the range's IN alphabet-name phrase (RangeAlphabet through TryResolveRangeAlphabet, COBOL0900 below 2002). Probed at --std 85: condition, arithmetic-expression, literal and TRUE/FALSE subjects, NOT with and without a THROUGH range of expressions, ANY, a nested EVALUATE and the period-terminated form compile and run. PARTIAL for one arm: evaluateWhenItem's partialExpression alternative has no edition gate, so a partial expression as a selection object (WHEN > 3, WHEN NOT < 3, WHEN NUMERIC, and a bare class-name) compiles and runs at 85. The 1985 object list has no such alternative, and §2002:F.2 item 48 records it as the 2002 change ("A partial expression may now be used as a selection object in an EVALUATE statement."); the row's change record names it among what 1985 refused. kb/Work PB398 (landed) added the alternative and wrote that it and the IN phrase were 2002 additions needing the edition-gate sweep; only the IN phrase got its gate. The witness runs five EVALUATE statements over the 1985 object forms.

next.reason: 1985: "[NOT] {identifier-3|literal-3|arithmetic-expression-1} [THROUGH|THRU {identifier-4|literal-4|arithmetic-expression-2}]"; 2023: "[ NOT ] boolean-expression-2 … partial-expression-1 … range-expression … [ IN alphabet-name-1 ]". Same EVALUATE format, but 2023 adds boolean-expression subjects and objects, partial-expression objects and IN alphabet-name on ranges, so it accepts programs 1985 refused.
